text:
A: Hiya! Hello, I'm Gemma. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah. Courtney.
A: Courtney. Lovely. I'm in Beeston, near Nottingham. Where are you?
B: Sunderland.
A: Ooh, I've never been. We went to Durham once for a wedding, does that count? Probably not, sorry.
B: Not really, no.
A: [laughs] No, fair enough. Erm, I love your hoodie, by the way, the little moth. I noticed it in your photo.
B: Thanks. It's Primark.
A: Well, it's a good Primark. What do you do, are you at uni?
B: No. Admin. Lettings office, part-time.
A: Oh, right, sorry, I just assumed. I'm part-time as well, I'm a pharmacy technician at the hospital. Three days. Do you like it, the lettings?
B: It's fine. It pays for stuff.
A: That's honest! Erm, sorry, I'm going to be really nosy, were those your drawings on the wall behind you?
B: Yeah.
A: I thought so! I can't draw at all, I'm terrible. I've just started pottery, though, night classes, and I've got a whole shelf of mugs that lean. Like, every single one leans a bit to the left, I don't know what I'm doing with my hands. Rob says they look like they've had a drink.
B: [laughs] Do you glaze them yourself?
A: Yeah! That's the best bit. I did one blue and green, and it came out of the kiln sort of brown, and I was gutted.
B: Glaze does that. It's like, you never really know until it's fired. I like that, though. Wonky stuff's better than shop stuff. Everything in the shops looks the same. If it leans, at least someone made it.
A: Oh, that's a lovely way of putting it. I'm going to tell Rob that.
B: He'll still think they're drunk.
A: [laughs] He will. What do you draw, then?
B: Ink stuff. Hands, moths, faces that turn into plants. I was talking to someone earlier about drawing old people's hands, actually. They're the best ones.
A: Oh, I see a lot of old hands on the wards! Thin skin, all the veins. Erm, did you study it? Art?
B: A-level. Started a Fine Art degree in Newcastle. Left in first year.
A: Oh, I did that! Biomedical Science at Sheffield Hallam, left after first year. I still think about it, to be honest, whether I wasted it.
B: Yeah. Same.
A: I got there in the end, though, sort of sideways, through work. So it's not over, do you know what I mean? You're what, twenty-one?
B: Yeah.
A: Duck, you've got loads of time. Sorry, I sound like your mam now.
B: Bit, yeah.
A: [laughs] Sorry! I'll stop.
B: It's fine. Send us a picture of the mugs.
A: Only if you send me a moth.
